front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《23》

en: Pushing imagination open
Flying into E = MC squared
A sky full of dazzling starlight

points.zh:
Albert Einstein:
“Imagination is more important than knowledge. For knowledge is limited, whereas
imagination embraces the entire world, stimulating progress, giving birth to evolution. "
In physics, mass–energy equivalence states that anything having mass has an equivalent amount of energy and vice versa, with these fundamental quantities directly relating to one another by Albert Einstein’s famous formula:    E = MC2
{\textstyle E=mc^{2}}This formula states that the equivalent energy (E) can be calculated as the mass (m) multiplied by the speed of light (c = about 3×108 m/s) squared. Similarly, anything having energy exhibits a corresponding mass m given by its energy E divided by the speed of light squared c². Because the speed of light is a very large number in everyday units, the formula implies that even an everyday object at rest with a modest amount of mass has a very large amount of energy intrinsically. Chemical, nuclear, and other energy transformations may cause a system to lose some of its energy content (and thus some corresponding mass), releasing it as the radiant energy of light or as thermal energy for example.    (from Wikipedia)

en: The affairs of the world are like a game of chess
An unfinished game, quietly kept watch over
A lone lamp, a moon's shadow?
Fog, vast and indistinct
Deep within, hidden
A lifetime's promise

zh: 江清月近的構圖已完成
en: The composition of clear river and near moon is already complete
Then wait for the fishing boat, following the bell's toll
Swaying into falling starlight

points.zh:
移舟泊烟渚，日暮客愁新。
野曠天低樹，江清月近人。
-- 唐。孟浩然《宿建德江》
points.en:
I moor my boat by a misty islet; as dusk falls, new sorrows rise for the traveler.
The wilds are vast, the sky lower than the trees; the river is clear, the moon draws near.
-- Tang dynasty. Meng Haoran, 'Staying Overnight on the Jiande River'

en: So be it, just let the flowers
Falling, adrift in the wind
Returning geese fly into the dusk
Now and then, there is also another voice
Answer me
Even if, only now and then
A temple
A quiet faith
The black-robed priest, half-hidden in the slanting sun
That is the withered vine
That is the crow at dusk, I follow
Ma Zhiyuan wanders to the ends of the earth

points.zh:
枯藤，老樹，昏鴉
小橋，流水，人家
古道，西風，瘦馬
夕陽西下，斷腸人在天涯
--元。馬致遠《天净沙 · 秋思》
points.en:
Withered vines, an old tree, a crow at dusk,
a small bridge, flowing water, a house,
an ancient road, the west wind, a gaunt horse,
the sun sets in the west,
a heartbroken man at the edge of the world.
-- Yuan dynasty. Ma Zhiyuan, 'Tian Jing Sha: Autumn Thoughts'

en: When it blooms, it blooms
When it drifts and falls, it drifts and falls
That's just how it is, the tung blossoms of May
Walking to where the water ends, sitting still
Vivaldi's "The Four Seasons"
Rising and drifting with the clouds and mist

points.zh:
中歲頗好道，晚家南山陲。 興來每獨往，勝事空自知。
行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。 偶然值林叟，談笑無還期。
--唐。王維《終南別業》
韋瓦第（Antonio Lucio Vivaldi，1678－1741）是出生在威尼斯的義大利人，水都威尼斯是一個極為浪漫又充滿了音樂的城市。當時的義大利已經發展成巴洛克時期的歐洲音樂重鎮，天時、地利正好孕育韋瓦第偉大的音樂。韋瓦第流傳後世最傑出的音樂類型為「歌劇」以及「協奏曲」，在他眾多協奏曲中，最傑出也最知名的一首當屬「四季」小提琴協奏曲。在將近三百年後的今日，這首曲子聽起來還是那麼新穎，完全掙脫時空對它的束縛，是人類偉大的音樂藝術資產。「四季」是小提琴協奏曲，標題分別是第一號「春」、第二號「夏」、第三號「秋」、第四號「冬」，每一號由標準的協奏曲快、慢、快三個樂章構成。換句話說，「四季」其實是四首獨立的三樂章小提琴協奏曲，但是因主題（季節）的相關性而被看成一組作品，統稱為「四季」。音樂搭配著十四行詩而進行，內容以四季的獨特景觀為描寫對象。
points.en:
In my middle years I came to love the Way; in old age I made my home at the foot of Zhongnan Mountain. When the mood strikes, I go off alone; the finest moments are known only to myself.
I walk until the water runs out, then sit and watch the clouds rise. By chance I meet an old man of the forest; we talk and laugh, with no thought of when to return.
-- Wang Wei (Tang dynasty), "My Retreat at Mount Zhongnan"
Vivaldi (Antonio Lucio Vivaldi, 1678-1741) was an Italian born in Venice. Venice, the city of water, is an extremely romantic city full of music. At that time, Italy had already developed into a major center of European Baroque music, and the confluence of favorable timing and place nurtured Vivaldi's great music. The musical genres for which Vivaldi is best remembered by later generations are opera and the concerto; among his many concertos, the most outstanding and best known is the violin concerto set "The Four Seasons." Nearly three hundred years later, this music still sounds fresh today, having completely broken free of the constraints of time and place -- it is a great treasure of human musical art. "The Four Seasons" consists of violin concertos titled No. 1 "Spring," No. 2 "Summer," No. 3 "Autumn," and No. 4 "Winter," each composed of the standard fast-slow-fast three-movement concerto structure. In other words, "The Four Seasons" is actually four independent three-movement violin concertos, but because of the thematic connection (the seasons), they are regarded as a single set of works and collectively called "The Four Seasons." The music is paired with accompanying sonnets, whose content depicts the distinctive scenery of each season.
